A glossy top coat might be your idea of perfection, while a hint of shimmer feels more you. There’s no wrong answer here. Ahead, some ideas for the best engagement nails to wear while you celebrate, from the soft, understated shades that let your ring do the talking to the bolder finishes that show off your personality.

A milky white manicure is anything but boring. It’s soft, sheer, and quietly luminous, with a clean, polished finish that makes your hands look effortlessly put together.

Delicate yet eye-catching, this manicure catches the light in all the right ways, making it a romantic choice that complements your ring without ever competing with it.

Another shade that plays into the holiday season, this metallic silver manicure brings a cool, icy shimmer to your engagement look. Sleek and glamorous, it pairs beautifully with platinum and white gold bands and makes a diamond sparkle even brighter.

#6661. Why Weed Might Actually Be Bad for Your Sleep

Everyone’s done it before. A pre-game gummy. A nighttime toke. Weed is, at this point, a widely used sleep aid. It usually works pretty well, too. But if you’ve made it a habit, you might just be sabotaging your shut-eye in the long run. According to a new October 2026 study, consuming pot in any form before bed causes people to have poorer quality of sleep—without them even realizing it. In other words: It has exactly the opposite of its intended effect. Here’s what you should know before popping an edible before you doze off.

The study, which was performed by Northwestern University researchers and published in JAMA Network, looked at 1,266 adults who participated in the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study, which followed participants for 35 years to determine how behavioral, biological, and environmental factors affected their risk of heart disease later in life. Of that sample size, 891 wore wrist-based activity monitors for at least a week so that researchers could examine their sleep patterns. After analyzing the data, the researchers found that those who were long-term cannabis users had “poorer objective sleep, including lower sleep efficiency, greater fragmentation, and more time awake during the night,” Dr. Thanh-Huyen Vu, an author of the study and a research associate professor of preventive medicine at Northwestern University’s Feinberg School of Medicine, tells GQ.

Here’s what all of that means: Sleep efficiency is essentially how much of the time you spend in bed you’re actually asleep. So, lower sleep efficiency means spending more time lying awake instead of sleeping while sleep fragmentation refers to how often your sleep is interrupted, like when you’re unknowingly tossing and turning to get comfortable. The researchers also looked at how much total time participants spent awake during the night. It all boils down to the fact that long-term cannabis users weren’t sleeping as soundly or as continuously throughout the night—sometimes without them even knowing it.

The researchers can’t say for certain. Because the study was observational, it only established an association between long-term cannabis exposure and poorer sleep quality.

One possibility, Vu suggests, is that cannabis may “alter normal sleep architecture,” potentially changing the way the body cycles through different sleep stages.

Over time, it’s those changes that can contribute to more nighttime awakenings, which result in less restorative sleep. She says more research is needed to understand the underlying biological mechanisms.

Deep sleep is one of the most important stages of sleep because it’s the phase when your body recovers physically, processes memory, and regulates the immune system. Interruptions in sleep result in less time during the deep sleep cycle, which inhibits your body from doing all the important things that help you function properly when you’re awake. The less deep sleep you get, the worse you feel in the morning. The reason why participants don’t pick up on these mid-sleep wake-ups is that they’re easy to forget. “Sleep trackers can capture some of these patterns, even when people don’t perceive their sleep as being particularly poor,” Vu says. It’s the same way in which you think you slept eight hours one night but woke up feeling groggy regardless.

Not necessarily. Given the sample population—middle-aged adults—the results may not apply to people in other age ranges or even those who use cannabis for medical reasons. Still, Vu says it’s important for people to understand that cannabis’s relationship with sleep may be more complicated than simply helping you drift off faster.

If you regularly use cannabis before bed, paying attention to your sleep patterns may help you better understand how it’s affecting you. Wearable sleep trackers can offer some insight into nighttime awakenings and sleep efficiency, but you won’t get the same sleep analysis if you were part of a study like this. It might be worth trying out a period where you don’t use weed to fall asleep to see if it makes a difference in whether you feel more well-rested, or your mind feels sharper. Though the study still leaves a lot of questions to be answered, its data is clear enough to make anyone with a nightly gummy habit reconsider.

#6660. Broiled Salmon Teriyaki

Sometimes all it takes to make dinner feel special is a big, bold piece of protein. Case in point: This salty-sweet salmon glazed in a glossy teriyaki-style sauce. Brushed in two rounds with the quick sauce made with nothing more than sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and vinegar, the salmon sizzles under the broiler, charring as it takes on a smoky flavor. This recipe calls for one large piece of salmon, but you can use smaller fillets or opt for a white fish such as cod or halibut. Just note that the cooking time will be shorter if using smaller pieces, so keep an eye on them. Add a quick garnish of sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds, and dinner is done.

More salmon winners this way: Hot Honey-Glazed Salmon; Green Curry-Glazed Salmon; and Slow-Roasted Salmon With Harissa.

Bring ⅓ cup (packed; 67 g) dark brown sugar, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp. unseasoned rice vinegar, and 2 tsp. toasted sesame oil to a simmer in a small saucepan over medium-high heat; cook until reduced by half and syrupy, 5–7 minutes. Let sauce cool until thickened slightly, about 10 minutes.

Heat broiler (if broiler is in your oven, place rack in upper third). Season both sides of one 1½–2-lb. skinless or skin-on center-cut salmon fillet with kosher salt. Place, skin side down, in a skillet or baking dish. Transfer one third of sauce to a small bowl and set aside for serving. Brush about half of remaining sauce over fillet. (If the salmon has a lot of room around it in the pan, line with foil to prevent runoff sauce from burning onto pan.)

Broil salmon until sauce is just starting to burn in spots, 4–7 minutes. Brush remaining sauce over fillet and broil until deeply charred and salmon is opaque all the way through, about 5 minutes.

Remove fish from oven and spoon reserved sauce over. Top with thinly sliced scallions and/or toasted sesame seeds if desired.

#6656. Should You Worry About That Bump on Your Chest?

If you’re like most guys, you probably have plenty of little bumps and lumps on your skin. There’s the callus on your toe from training for that 10K, the razor bumps along your neck from this morning’s shave, and the skin tag on your underarm you keep meaning to get removed. While it’s often completely fine to ignore these bumps, that isn’t always the case. Some can be a red flag worth paying attention to—especially if they’re on your chest.

While male breast cancer is rare, estimates suggest that more than 2,600 men are diagnosed with an invasive form of the disease each year in the United States, and more than 500 die, according to the American Cancer Society. And one of its telltale signs is a firm bump under or near your nipple. Below, find out more about what a breast-cancer lump may look like and four other things that could be to blame for a new bump on your chest.

There isn’t a universal description of what breast cancer lumps look like in men, but there are some common characteristics to keep in mind. “Breast cancer in men typically presents as a painless, firm, or hard lump,” says Jose Pablo Leone, MD, the director of the Program for Breast Cancer in Men at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston.

Another sign that the bump could be breast cancer is if it’s behind or very close to the nipple and areola. “Men have much less developed breast glandular tissue than women, which is why breast cancer in men most commonly develops near or behind the nipple,” says Dr. Leone. As for size even a lump as small as a pea can be cancerous, but by the time men go to the doctor, tumors are often larger than a marble, according to Dr. Leone. “In part because of the lack of awareness and screening, most men present with larger tumors,” he says. “But any size is worth mentioning to your doctor. Not all breast cancers feel the same, so any new or persistent breast lump should be evaluated by a healthcare professional.”

Your chest has a lot of oil glands, which can set the stage for pimples. “Staying in a sweaty shirt after a workout can make chest acne flare, especially if the fabric is tight and rubs against your skin,” says Elizabeth Bahar Houshmand, MD, a board-certified dermatologist based in Dallas. While blackheads and whiteheads are typically small and easy to identify, inflamed pimples or nodules may seem more alarming because they can be hard, painful, and form deep under the skin. When it comes to nodular acne specifically, you can’t treat it on your own. If that’s what you think you’re dealing with, see a dermatologist, who can prescribe an oral or topical medication to help clear it up.

“This is a collection of fat that forms under the skin,” says Sonya Kenkare, MD, a board-certified dermatologist at Illinois Dermatology Institute in Hinsdale, Illinois. “It is usually soft, not painful, and you can move it around in all different directions.” You don’t need to do anything about a lipoma, but if you want to get it removed, you can talk to a doctor about it.

When hair follicles get inflamed or infected, you can end up with folliculitis. “Folliculitis often looks like small pimples or pus-filled bumps centered around a hair follicle” says Dr. Houshmand. “They may itch or feel tender.”

Blockage or damage to a hair follicle can also cause epidermal inclusion cysts. These cysts occur when dead skin cells get trapped under the surface instead of shedding. “They feel somewhat firm and often have a central little black spot,” says Dr. Kenkare. Sometimes simply applying a warm compress to the area can help a cyst heal on its own, but a doctor can also inject it with a steroid to reduce swelling, drain it, or surgically remove it.

This condition occurs when breast tissue gets enlarged in men, and it can first appear as a lump under your nipple. “It often feels like a rubbery or firm disc beneath the nipple, and it may be tender,” says Dr. Houshmand. While gynecomastia can come on as a side effect of some medications, like antibiotics or antidepressants, or diseases like thyroid disorders, sometimes there is no clear cause at all.

If you’re starting to feel like it’s difficult to tell on your own what the lump on your chest might be, you’re not wrong. That’s why it’s best to have your primary care physician look at any new, unexplained bumps and tell you whether you need imaging, like a mammogram with an ultrasound. That may sound scary, but it’s really just covering your bases. “Uncommon things are uncommon, and breast cancer in men is uncommon,” says Dr. Leone. “You shouldn’t worry excessively about male breast cancer, but you should be aware of it.”

#6655. Why Is Fashion So Obsessed With Distressing?

In 2026, fashion is getting messy with distressing.

In 2026, the runways are ripe with notes of distressing and deconstruction. For fall/winter 2026, Prada sent crystal-covered embellished heels down the runway with perfectly pointed toes that looked as if they had just accidentally graced a puddle of distinctly dirty New York City rainwater. The same is true for the label’s menswear collections: deliberate stains, frayed fabrics, and wrinkles were intentional and core to the aesthetic. At Miu Miu and Coach, leathers were aged. And for spring/summer 2027, Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Valentino, Diesel, and JW Anderson showcased elements of worn-in style, with damaged, repaired, dirty, and distressed looks dominating. After seasons of quiet luxury defined by minimal, poised, and perfected aesthetics, something about fashion’s new love affair with mess feels refreshing.

With 2008 fashion on the rise, too, maybe we’re closer than we ever thought to going back to ripped jeans. Ann Demeulemeester, Balenciaga, and Diesel seem to think so, as all of these labels put frayed jeans on the runway for the spring/summer 2027 season. Ann Demeulemeester creative director Stefano Gallici brainstormed his new collection on a journey through the Californian desert, and in the show notes mentioned intentional wear, via “Ceremony tailoring worn to death, or to eternity.”

But why is fashion obsessed with looking worn out right now? Valerie Steele, director and chief curator of The Museum at the Fashion Institute of Technology, thinks there’s never been a better time for it. “There is kind of a crisis in fashion right now,” she tells ELLE. “Fashion has started to seem really out of touch with real life and real people.” One example: luxury fashion’s pricing is so high right now that some brands, like Gucci, have announced that they’ll be reducing prices by as much as 30 percent. Also: “There is kind of more of an interest in what ‘real people’ wear. You know, what does it mean to be authentic? I mean, in many ways, I would say that authenticity is a chimera. You know, it’s a mythical beast that doesn’t really exist in a totally commodified, late capitalist world,” says Steele.

Steele notes the damaged jeans of the Y2K era, ’90s grunge moments, and earlier punk movements as similar examples. Deliberate distressing has also been famously done and documented by some of the greats, like Vivienne Westwood, Rei Kawakubo, and even Alber Elbaz, also coinciding with unique moments in time when economics and politics made it all the more interesting and, in some cases, ironic. “Fashion is supposed to be new and transgressive,” says Steele. “So, if scuffing your shoes is gonna make them more fashionable, then you go for it, right?”

Intentionally distressed, messy fashion has been around for hundreds of years, however. “We also saw it actually with some male dandies in the second half of the 19th century,” says Steele. “You also had some of that sensibility in New England in the late 19th century when wealthy people in Boston would go to Paris and buy their couture clothes, and then they just keep them in a trunk for a year, so they wouldn’t be so new when they were worn for the first time. It has a lot to do with the idea that the sort of shiny newness of fashion may seem a little bit fashion victim-y. They weren’t having to show off that it was brand new.”

In case there was any doubt that the distressed effect is just another example of insular runway fashion, people are actually buying ripped, stained, destroyed clothes outside of the designer space, too. Just look at Distressed Fest, a biannual, bicoastal vintage clothing pop-up event focused on heavily worn, threadbare, and destroyed garments that are sold for a premium. Scuffs, rips, stains, and all: as ironic as it may be, fashion’s current status symbol now is looking like you’ve been through something.

#6654. Chili Crisp Yogurt Chicken

Slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior. But the best part of this sheet-pan dinner comes after the chicken is cooked: Spread cooked rice into the pan’s juices, then slide the baking sheet back into the oven. As the rice soaks up the deeply savory sauce, it will crisp in spots, creating a texture that’s somewhere between chewy-fluffy steamed grains and a freshly toasted pita chip. And when it comes to chili crisp, we love the iconic and easy-to-source Lao Gan Ma, but specialty brands like Fly By Jing are great too—just make sure the one you use is not too spicy, which will overpower the dish.

More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.

Preheat oven to 425°. Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Whisk together ¾ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt and ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp in a large bowl. Add chicken thighs and toss to coat.

Arrange chicken on a rimmed baking sheet and top with any yogurt mixture left in bowl. Bake chicken until deeply browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh registers 165°, 25–30 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate.

Spread 3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice over baking sheet with chicken juices and bake until most of the juices have been absorbed and rice is starting to crisp in spots, 12–15 minutes.

Meanwhile, whisk together 1 Tbsp. finely grated lime zest, ¼ cup fresh lime juice, ½ tsp. sugar, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and remaining ¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt in a small bowl.

Combine ½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced, and a big pinch of Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using your hands, scrunch cabbage gently to soften. Add 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, 1 cup finely chopped cilantro, and yogurt dressing and toss to combine. Taste cabbage slaw and season with more salt if needed.

Slice chicken as desired and serve with crisped rice and cabbage slaw.

#6653. The Berkshires Are Made for a Soft-Life Getaway

Two hours from New York City, this corner of Massachusetts pairs farm-fresh finds and open-air beauty with restorative retreats

Every Saturday from May to November, Great Barrington has a popular farmers’ market. Lines of local Berkshirites, visitors, little kids, and friendly dogs on leashes gather under packed canopies to buy a vibrant mix of fresh fruits, vegetables, flowers, and more. An older woman overheard me talking to my husband—in town for our end-of-summer vacation—about honeycrisps and insisted we go to the opposite end of the market to Maynard Farms’s booth. The family-owned orchard carries a diverse range of apples and “amazing stone fruits” she swore our excitable toddlers would love. She was right—the boys devoured nearly all of the produce before we left the market.

Last August, in the final warm days of summer, we drove winding highways through Hudson River mountains to the westernmost area of Massachusetts: a lush and culturally rich destination composed of 30 towns and two cities, collectively known as the Berkshires and located just two hours outside of New York City.

Lenox, the town we stayed in, is a quaint enclave that boasts multimillion-dollar Cape Cods, luxury day resorts, golfing, country clubs, and farm-to-table restaurants. It’s an ideal place for a weekend getaway with friends, a romantic escape, or a family trip with your littles to touch well-landscaped grass.

We stayed in a newly built rental home, directly across the street from the Boston Symphony Orchestra at Tanglewood. In the evenings, if you’re within three miles of the parking lot, you can hear concerts from world-renowned artists. “Whether you're sitting in the front row enjoying James Taylor in the Koussevitzky Music Shed or sharing a candlelit picnic under the stars on the lawn, there is something magical about being here,” says Amy Aldrich, senior director of patron experience at Tanglewood. “We take great pride in creating a welcoming atmosphere where world-class music and the beauty of nature come together to create something truly special.”

Well-to-do families have long escaped the hustle of metropolitan New England cities to decompress in the Berkshires because of its natural beauty. Author Edith Wharton, who chronicled the sordid lives of Gilded Age elites, built her 16,000-square-foot mansion and expansive garden estate in Lenox in 1902.

Back in the day, when affluent housewives needed a respite, they’d go to the “spa.” I never fully understood the older meaning of the term until I visited Miraval Berkshires, a 380-acre resort that boasts ancient Eastern treatments, healing equine therapy sessions, meditation classes, macronutrient dining, sound baths, astrological readings, and much more. It’s an adults-only, device-free space, so disconnecting from stress is mandatory.

Equestrian activities were a common theme for us during the trip. HomeFarm at Undermountain, run by executive director Lori Pestana, is a gem of a property. The animal sanctuary is dedicated to caring for and maintaining the health of horses—but also houses goats, sheep, and donkeys. “It’s a place where life slows down, where people reconnect with nature, with animals, and often with themselves,” Pestana says. “Whether visitors come to ride, explore, learn, or simply experience the peaceful rhythm of farm life, they leave with something they didn’t necessarily know they were looking for—a sense of belonging, joy, and connection.”

Pestana’s small but dedicated staff offers riding lessons and a holistic view of what restoration can look like with a lot of care.

For dining, expect most restaurants to serve farm-to-table dishes that are sourced from the seasonal produce and livestock being raised in the area. You couldn’t possibly get a closer farm-to-table experience than Highlawn Farms, which has delicious cheeses, ice cream, and milk made from the same cows grazing its property. It’s a general rule of thumb in my family that we never pass up the opportunity to have a wood-fired pizza—Pizzeria Boema has a chic Scandinavian interior and New England quaint courtyard, serving the crispy, flavor-filled pies made with locally sourced mozzarella. And if you’re more interested in a fine-dining experience, Cello, run by couple Ryan and Kim Boya, takes a contemporary approach to comfort food. The 29-seat intimate restaurant has a thoughtfully curated menu of autochthonous plates like oyster mushroom pappardelle and a honey-nut squash served with goat cheese, pickled poblanos, granola, and a drizzle of hot honey.

Wildlife is ever-present in the Berkshires, from the calming transparently clear waters of Lenox Beach to the newly renovated aquarium wing of the Berkshire Museum in Pittsfield. Out the window of our car, driving from town to town, we saw peaceful creeks, grazing deer, and chirping birds. I soaked it all in, even stopping at the side of Glendale Road in Stockbridge to take in the beauty of the Housatonic River.

In recent years, because of the chaos of flying with toddlers, I’ve come to really appreciate the convenience of going to places just outside of New York City. I just want a soft life—or one as soft as humanly possible. With a good playlist on deck (we lean toward Afrojazz or Bad Bunny), we strap the kids into their car seats and roll. Open space and calm have to be on the itinerary.

There are many places we could go, but this experience in the Berkshires really stuck with me because it offered a quiet luxury that doesn’t position itself as high-maintenance or arrogant. There’s an ease and openness to this place, and if nothing else, an amazing peck of apples I’ll be looking forward to on my next visit.

#6652. How Did This 14-Year-Old Get Sam Bankman-Fried on the Phone?

Journalists who’ve been anxious about losing their jobs to artificial intelligence would be wise to focus on a different, altogether less menacing but equally impressive threat: 14-year-old Eli Goldfine, the shoestring podcaster from Westchester County who last week conducted a 90-minute interview with Sam Bankman-Fried, who’s currently serving a 25-year sentence in federal prison for orchestrating a multi-billion-dollar cryptocurrency grift.

So how, exactly, does this precocious ninth grader with braces—and not a reporter from one of the scores of legacy publications who’d surely be gunning for access to the disgraced cryptocurrency king—score an interview so coveted? “I had written about Sam on Twitter a little bit, and it got picked up by the person who was at the time running Sam’s account,” Goldfine, who hosts a podcast about prediction markets called The Supercycle, told me earlier this week. “I think they were impressed with my knowledge of various parts of his criminal case.”

Goldfine’s classmates are impressed, too, even though he’s been on the receiving end of some gentle ribbing about his on-air ad reads. But can any of them say they got Bankman-Fried to speculate on the likelihood that AI will bring about the extinction of the human race? ("Less than 50%, more than 10%," by the way). Before school’s out for Thanksgiving break, Goldfine joined GQ to talk about his media diet, dream interview subject, and the mechanics of interviewing a man behind bars.

Okay. So my podcast is primarily about prediction markets and other broader markets. And I got into that during the 2024 election. So I learned more about it and I started trading on a fake-money version of Polymarket.

It's called Manifold Markets. And what's cool about that one is, anyone can create their own question rather than the platform deciding. I mean, probably not. I don't have anything against it per se, because people spend money for entertainment on other things. I mean, this is another way to spend your money. #6651. The Most Flattering Hairstyles for Women Over 50, From Bobs to Long Layers

The most flattering styles are less about age and more about shape, movement, and hair health.

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

The rules are relative when it comes to “age-appropriate hair.” No matter what decade you’re presently thriving in, the style you choose should make you feel good. That said, as hair texture, volume, and color change with age, some styles may feel and look better once you hit your 50s. The options are vast, but don’t think you have to go shorter as you mature or cover up sprouting grays. If anything, feel free to experiment. Worn short hair all your life? Try some extensions and waist-length waves. Or if you’ve had long hair for as long as you can remember, trim a few inches off into a happy medium lob. Experts share tips and ideas for choosing the best hairstyle if you’re over 50.

The most important thing is to choose for the hair you have now. “I tell my clients to think about things like fullness, movement, tone, and shape,” Elba Iris, John Frieda stylist and educator, tells ELLE. A good style, Elba adds, should make hair look healthy and as full as possible, have movement so it never looks stiff or set, and have shine with dimension. It’s also helpful to be realistic about your routine and consider how much daily effort and time you can commit to styling your hair.

Also, keep in mind that length is a personal choice. “One thing I really dislike is when women are told they need to cut their hair after a certain age,” says Rodger Azadganian, a hairstylist, salon owner, and founder of Äz Haircare. “I think that’s such an outdated idea. I care much more about the condition of the hair and whether the cut suits the person. If you love long hair, keep it long,” he encourages. Iris completely agrees, adding that shape, health, shine, and confidence are what make your hair look youthful.

Azadganian is a huge fan of a sharp bob, which he says always looks sophisticated. “I also love collarbone-length hair with a little movement around the face. And I think long, beautiful hair on a woman over 50 can be incredibly chic,” he adds.

Iris says the styles that consistently flatter his over-50 clients are those with softness around the face, deep angles, and layers if the hair is longer. Like Azadganian, Iris also says a collarbone-length lob with long soft layers is the most versatile. “It keeps length, gives movement, and [can be] styled in various ways,” says Iris. He adds that a textured bob, worn a little undone rather than perfectly smooth, is chic at any age and makes fine hair look thicker because the ends are blunt and full.

If you have or prefer short hair, Iris says a soft pixie with a longer, swept fringe is beautiful and lifts the whole face. “Face-framing layers or a soft curtain fringe are my secret weapon—they draw the eye up, soften everything, and grow out gracefully between appointments.”

Gray hair grows in with a different texture than you may be used to. It’s often wirier, drier, and more resistant to products and color, so styles may need more moisture and smoothing than before.

For those who dye their hair all one color and have started to, or are already fully gray, regrowth may pose an unflattering problem. “Solid color against graying regrowth creates a harsh line and can actually make thinning at the part more visible,” Iris cautions. Instead, both Iris and Azadganian recommend dimensional color over anything too flat or solid. Go for softer dimension—highlights, lowlights, or a blended “gray blending” approach. This technique diffuses the regrowth, adds the illusion of depth and fullness, and buys you more time between appointments.

If you’re embracing grey fully, love it. The key, though, according to Iris, is to keep it bright and conditioned. “Grey hair can yellow and look dull; a glossing treatment and the right purple shampoo, like John Frieda Violet Crush, keep it silver and striking instead of dusty. Color should work with your styling, never make it harder,” Iris recommends.

For fine hair, both Azadganian and Iris suggest keeping the ends blunt in order to make the hair look fuller. “A bob or lob with a strong perimeter makes hair look twice as dense, and I’d avoid heavy layering, which removes the fullness you can see. Fullness also has to be built at the styling,” Iris explains. He recommends the John Frieda Ultra Filler+ shampoo and conditioner for fine hair to plump each strand and to make hair look and feel thicker when styled. Use a thickening spray at the root before blow-drying for lasting lift.

For thick or coarse hair, go with longer layers to take out some weight and keep it from looking heavy and triangular. For curly and coily hair, Iris says shape is key. “A cut done on dry hair, in its natural state, with layers that let the curl sit where it lives, plus real moisture.”

Azadganian says a beautifully shaped curly bob is incredible. “I always want the haircut to work with the texture instead of forcing it into something else,” he notes.

Wavy hair looks best in a mid-length cut with soft layers that enhance the natural bend of the texture without heat styling. As for length, Iris says short hair loves texture and a little messiness. “Mid-length, chin to collarbone, is the sweet spot for most women because it’s long enough to feel feminine and short enough to stay full,” says Iris. Long hair after 50 absolutely works, but as both stylists noted, only if the hair is kept healthy and styled.

Azadganian says one of the biggest mistakes with hair over age 50 is getting stuck with the same hairstyle for decades. “You don’t need to change everything, but even updating your layers, fringe, or part can make such a difference. I love seeing women experiment with their hair at every age,” says Azadganian.

#6650. 15 Places to Donate This Holiday Season

The act of gift-giving always seems incredibly fun before the holidays come around. But I doubt I’m the only one who has suddenly come to in a sweaty, consumerist panic after all the presents are unwrapped and there is wrapping paper and ribbon on the floor, wishing I’d put my money somewhere meaningful instead of showering my little cousins with books they are exceedingly polite about but clearly hate.

That’s why, in recent years, I’ve made the decision to donate to an important cause in a loved one’s name—and I’ve never, ever regretted it. Below, find a roundup of some of the Vogue staff’s favorite organizations doing hard and necessary work that could use a little love this holiday season:

“I always give to the Red Cross in the wake of natural disasters, but this year the cause was a little closer to home when the organization stepped in to provide relief to those displaced by the terrible building collapse that took place in Flatbush earlier this month. I live near the building site, and for several nights, the entire neighborhood was kept awake by hovering helicopters, a terrible reminder of the tragedy that had occurred. There have been many initiatives since, organized by friends and neighbors, to provide assistance. But for those who might like to bolster the resilient spirit of New York City this holiday season from farther afield, a donation to the Red Cross would be worthwhile.” —Chloe Schama

“As someone who has always loved reading, I believe books have the power to open up new worlds, spark our imaginations, and inspire us to dream bigger. Every child deserves the opportunity to experience that same magic. Behind the Book brings diverse books and authors into underserved New York City public school classrooms, helping children discover the joy of reading and storytelling.” —Molly Barstein

Imagine a ticking clock: One person is diagnosed with cancer every 1.6 seconds worldwide, and the Breakthrough Board is a women’s coalition that has been funding life-saving cancer research at the University of Chicago for nearly 80 years. Vogue senior digital line editor Jane Chun recommends donating and/or volunteering your time for this worthy cause.

Many of us would be at a loss without our furry companions, so a donation to this animal welfare organization—which operates the largest no-kill animal shelter in the US in Kanab, Utah, and partners with shelters and rescue groups nationwide—is a particularly nice way to honor the beloved pet in your life.

United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has detained over 8,000 children and increased family separations under the Trump administration. A donation to this California-based nonprofit (which will be matched through the end of December) helps to support those children and families with critical legal resources, medical and psychological treatment, and other forms of sorely needed support.

This nonprofit organization, which will have Vogue Head of Editorial Content Chloe Malle’s support this year, has been helping people affected by conflict and disaster around the world for the past 90 years. It is currently matching donations for families in Gaza (times three) through Giving Tuesday.

Over 10 million older adults live in poverty in the US, and this organization—which was founded by a Philadelphia social worker in 1954—works to mitigate that sad state of affairs by delivering healthy, culturally sensitive meals (and needed social contact) to seniors around the country.

A donation to this organization attempting to find a cure for multiple myeloma (a type of blood cancer that forms in plasma cells) goes particularly far right now, notes Vogue Fashion Commerce Director Madeline Fass, as every dollar you give before December 31 will be doubled—up to $1 million—thanks to a special matching challenge from Dr. Elsey’s Fund to Cure Cancer.

With ICE raids and arrests ongoing all over the country, a donation to the Los Angeles-based National Day Laborer Organizing Network’s Immigrant Defense Fund helps to support legal defense and public advocacy for immigrant communities under attack.

The right to a safe, accessible abortion has only become more imperiled since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade in 2022, and this nonprofit network of over 100 independent, grassroots abortion funds is working to increase access and make sure no pregnant person is forced to go without potentially lifesaving care.

Federal funding for NPR, PBS, and local public media stations was ended by President Donald Trump in 2025, but you can step up and help fill the gap by donating directly to your local station to support independent journalism. “I plan to support my local NPR station, WNYC,” says Chloe Malle.

Nobody should be forced to navigate the aftermath of sexual assault or misconduct alone, and a donation to the Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network (RAINN) helps fund vital services like the organization’s national 24-hour sexual assault hotline to ensure that survivors always have somewhere to turn.

There are tons of great organizations working to end hunger in the US, from Feeding America to Feed the Children, but sometimes it’s nice to find one working locally. For New Yorkers, that might just be this Harlem-based nonprofit that serves 900 free, chef-prepared meals a week to community members facing hunger.

It’s a scary time for trans, nonbinary, and gender-nonconforming youth in the US, which makes a donation to this mutual aid project serving unhoused and/or vulnerable trans youth (or a gift purchased directly from someone’s registry) particularly meaningful.

“I plan to adopt a couple of snowy owls for the children in my life through the World Wildlife Fund,” says Malle—and you, too, can help prevent the vulnerable species’s extinction (while nabbing yourself a snowy owl plush toy) by donating to the WWF.

#6647. These Perfumes Are Basically Main Character Energy in a Bottle

Discover the scents that turn an everyday entrance into a scene.

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

We’re all the main characters of our own lives, so why not step into the part with a fragrance that makes you feel like one?

When studied, main characters are often going through a transformation: change (Katniss Everdeen), personal growth (Elle Woods), or hardship (Andy Sachs). Almost all of them find their inner confidence by the end of the story, at least in the more true-to-life films.

That confidence is exactly what a great fragrance can help you channel. Scent is closely tied to memory and emotion, which is why a single spritz can shift your mood before you’ve even left the house. Think of it as your personal soundtrack: a warm vanilla and amber for your cozy, golden-hour scene, a crisp bergamot and white floral for the day you walk into the room ready to take charge, a smoky, woody blend for your mysterious entrance.

The right perfume can help you feel like the person you already are, only more so. Check out some of the fragrances below that instantly make you feel and step into main character energy.

She’s warm, spicy, and impossible to miss. This Kayali fragrance is for the main character who's confident, authentic, and entirely herself, bringing warmth to everyone around her.

She's an It girl by default. Chanel's Gabrielle captures the charming essence of Gabrielle "Coco" Chanel herself, before she created the House of Chanel. This floral fragrance is rich, feminine, and sparkling with freshness. It's perfect for go-getters who treasure chic in their lives.

Key Notes: Jasmine, Ylang-Ylang, Orange Blossom, Grasse Tuberose

#6645. GQ’s Best Gifts for Men 2026: 70+ Editor-Approved Presents

There's no shortage of stuff to buy for men. Stuff worth giving? That's another story. Fortunately, finding stuff worth giving is a salaried position around here. The results of that extensive retail research are all here: a carefully considered mix of great clothes, clever gadgets, handsome home goods, and a few things he probably wouldn't think to buy himself. We keep this guide updated throughout the year, so below you'll find our latest favorites alongside a few perennial heaters, all handpicked to make your gift-giving duties a little easier.

Still got names to cross off your list? Browse the rest of our gift guides and sign up for the GQ Recommends newsletter for a steady supply of good ideas.

This Banana Republic glen plaid double-breasted jacket features a rarely seen 2x1 button stance, which makes it a touch more casual but no less handsome.

Among Ralph Lauren's many contributions to American fashion is transforming the denim shirt from a Western novelty into a staple of the modern wardrobe. This weathered slub denim version is a handsome example, and something he'll wear for years to come.

Few knits occupy a place in the menswear pantheon quite like J.Crew's rollneck sweater. With its relaxed weave and raglan sleeves, it's an enduring heater that makes for an easy gift.

What makes Morjas' Belgian loafer so irresistible to those who've had the good fortune to wear it is just how comfortable it is. Doesn't hurt that it's also clean, understated, and versatile as all get-out.

Maple's Orbit bracelet is a great little way to add a fleck of personality to an otherwise understated fit. And if this design is a little too out-there for his taste, you may have to look elsewhere entirely. That's kind of Maple's whole thing.

Smaller, thinner cases are great, and the Timex Marlin is a stone-cold minimalist classic in that world. But it also sells out, so allow us to recommend another, newer Timex gem: the Marlin Jet Titanium. He'll love that it's an automatic, too.

Patagonia's Snap-T is an icon, and this new Re-Tool Air version gives it a fresh spin with an exclusive Polartec fleece that's remarkably lightweight, wonderfully warm, and made from 100% recycled polyester.

This merino wool crewneck from Arc'teryx is lightweight, great at regulating temperature, and just as good worn on its own as it is layered under a sweater or jacket. A go-to layering piece for just about any wardrobe.

If you ask us, the Moon Shoe is one of the Swoosh's best releases of the year. A perfectly retro, low-profile runner with a refreshingly affordable price tag.

A great hoodie is essential, and Reigning Champ nails fit-meets-function better than most, with an aesthetic inspired by old-school athletic training gear. This one is cut from the brand’s signature midweight terry, which is soft and substantial without feeling bulky.

A man can never have enough flannels. Filson's Rangeland is made from brushed 5.5-ounce cotton, and we're partial to the red and gray plaid.

Massachusetts-based Steele Canvas has been making sturdy canvas goods for generations, and its Everyday Tote is exactly the sort of gift they'll most definitely get some use out of.

When we think of field watches, we think of Hamilton. This no-nonsense mechanical number is hard to beat in the category, and you could spend a lot more on a lot less.

A good pair of cowboy boots can do wonders for a fit, and Tecovas' Warren makes a strong case for adding a little yee-haw to the rotation. With classic flame stitching and a sharp cutter toe, they're more versatile than you might think.

3sixteen's asymmetrical fleece is freaky, but not too freaky, with a wide boatneck, an off-center zipper at the neck, and an oversized pocket with a zip closure. There's a lot going on, but the proportions are spot-on.

Some of the best stuff Miansai makes is low-key its bead and stone jewelry. The Avi necklace is a welcome change of pace from the usual gold and silver.

John Smedley has been making knitwear in England for more than 200 years, and there's a reason it's still considered some of the best in the biz. This wool polo might look simple, but the quality of the knit, the fit, and the finishing make it something special.

OrSlow's 105 jeans have a classic straight leg and medium rise, with the kind of easy, timeless fit that never goes out of style. A very good upgrade for anyone whose denim rotation could use a little love.

Yes, it costs a pretty penny. But it also might be one of the coolest scarves we’ve ever seen: so robust you can wrap it around yourself a few times like a sweater, at which point the price starts to make more sense. Oh, and it’s Burberry.

Movado's iconic Museum Watch has been a masterclass in minimalism since 1947, with a Bauhaus-inspired dial that's blank save for a single dot at 12 o'clock. A remarkably sleek timepiece, especially at this price.

Some days call for a full wallet, others for just the essentials. Coach's 3-in-1 gives him both, with a removable ID insert that works just as well on its own when he wants to travel a little lighter.

For the record, we're all for giving socks as presents, provided they're of the same caliber as those from Japan's Rototo.

Quince is one of our first stops for affordable cashmere, but its merino wool offerings ain't too shabby either. Take this sweater, which it done up in cable-knit for a little somethin' somethin'.

Blundstone introduced its Heritage boot this year, a decidedly more upscale take on the brand's beloved Chelsea. Handmade from premium leather, it's also finished with a Goodyear welt that allows it to be resoled for years to come.

Come for the three iconic Byredo scents, which you can spritz according to whatever the mood calls for. Stay for the handsome leather case, which is almost reason enough to gift the set on its own.

Plenty of dopp kits come in sleek leather (no shade), and plenty of designer versions cost a small fortune (some shade). But most guys just want something that looks good and can take a beating on the road. Filson knows how to do that.

Bar soaps have officially entered the elevated grooming arena, with better ingredients and better scents. Made in France, this bar adds a pop of color by the tub, lathers like a dream, and carries Frama's gorgeous Herbarium aroma that lingers on skin long after the shower.

Bleu de Chanel's Parfum takes everything great about the original and turns it up a notch. Still zesty and botanical, but with sandalwood and tonka bean lending a richer, smoother finish.

Released this year, Braun's Nevo is arguably the best and most advanced foil shaver on the market today, and our own testing backs that up. Given the price tag, it's exactly the sort of splurge that makes for a great gift.

Vitamins B and C do wonders for the skin, and Aesop's B Triple C Facial Balancing Gel is packed with both. Deeply hydrating yet leaving a matte finish, it was a game changer when it debuted over 20 years ago, and it's still elite after all these years.

If he’s taking skincare cues from anyone, it should be Pharrell, who apparently doesn’t age. The multihyphenate’s skincare brand, Humanrace, has a Rejuvenating Face Mask featuring a peptide trio complex to keep your lucky guy looking chipper.

The Philips OneBlade 360 is a little groomer we love for its versatility. There’s really nothing quite like it out there, and it can handle just about any hairy situation.

Dior seems to drop a new olfactory banger every few months, and Bois d'Argent is one of the latest. Smooth woods, amber, and rich iris mingle with frankincense for a scent that's warm, elegant, and easy to wear just about anywhere.

Wonder Valley's newish Wild Garden hand wash puts olive oil to good use, whipping up a rich, softening lather with a cedar-and-herb scent that brings a little of the great outdoors to the sink.

A moisturizer is a no-brainer, but a serum signals one is getting extra serious about skincare. Caldera + Lab makes that addition easy: a few pumps deliver vitamin C, collagen amino acids, and skin-soothing botanicals to brighten, firm, and soften fine lines.

We've been longtime fans of Dr. Dennis Gross's Alpha Beta Universal Daily Peel pads, which make good skincare almost embarrassingly easy. A couple of swipes help exfoliate dead skin, smooth texture, and brighten the complexion.

Tower 28's travel-size SOS set packs everything they need to stay fresh on the go. A little skincare insurance for wherever the holidays take them.

Salt & Stone makes one of our favorite body washes, and this mini set lets them take the whole lineup for a spin.

With these hydrating eye patches from one of the best grooming brands to do it, no one will ever know he didn't get his proper eight hours last night.

You can buy all the fancy sunscreen you want, but convenience decides if you actually wear it. Freaks of Nature’s SPF 50 stick—small, glide-on, reef safe, and water-resistant for 80 minutes—nails it.

The LED mask market is booming, and Omnilux is at the top of the heap. This one is specifically designed and FDA-cleared for men’s typically thicker facial skin, targeting fine lines, firmness, and overall health, while helping calm any redness from shaving. In other words, it’s a Michael Myers-like mask that promises scary-good skin with consistency and patience.

Hair dryers have officially gotten techy-cool, and Laifen is a big part of it. The new SE 2 is so sleek and ergonomic, with intuitive controls to match, he'll want to leave it on display.

Smythson and Burberry joining forces is more British heritage than you can wave a Union Jack at. Smythson already makes a covetable travel chess set, but add Burberry's signature check and it's, well, checkmate.

ICYMI: Menswear's patron saint Todd Snyder linked up with West Elm for a stirring collection of homewares this past year, and the hands-down standout is this walnut valet chair. A handsome place to hang tomorrow's outfit—or yesterday's, if we're being realistic.

It's a tabletop lighter shaped like a mallard duck. Something you'd find in the study of a delightfully eccentric uncle, and exactly the sort of gift no one knows they want until they get one.

A speckled enamelware thermos from Polo Country, because why not.

Few brands have done more to make everyday essentials like bedding, towels, and sleepwear into objects of desire than Copenhagen's Tekla. Its PJs embody that sensibility: beautifully cut, made from crisp organic cotton, and available in a killer assortment colors and stripes.

I love this genre of slipper, the travel kind that zips into its own little case. And these from Luca come at an incredible price, with a perfectly shaped toe box and rubber soles that make them handsome enough to wear out.

If they're going to keep ordering pants off the internet, they might as well have a proper tool for opening all those packages. The Palmer knife makes short work of cardboard and packing tape, so they can get to the fit pics faster.

Hoto’s sleek PixelDrive electric screwdriver comes with 30 interchangeable bits and a nifty pixelated display that shows exactly how much power he’s working with. That wobbly dining chair doesn’t stand a chance.

This isn't one of those dinky makeup fridges. This is a countertop fridge fridge, the latest in beverage-holding innovation from Rocco. And of course, it looks great.

I picked up Nanu’s Arc earlier this year, and I’ve gotten way more joy out of it than I expected. It’s a well-built, thoughtfully engineered analog clock with a discreet digital display and a lovely mechanical chime. Not cheap, sure, but having one less reason to reach for my phone has been worth every penny.

Call me old-fashioned, but a man ought to know how to make a proper drink. And he ought to have the right tools for the job. Fellow's new eight-piece cocktail set has everything he needs to shake, stir, and strain his way to a good one.

It may come as a shock, but there's a whole world beyond burgers worth smashing. Caraway's immaculately designed grill press is up to the task.

A good set of bedsheets is a nice gift. An adult gift. It says, “I care about you, even when you're unconscious.” Parachute's brushed cotton sheets are those sheets: soft, cozy, and something they'll appreciate every single night.

Shinola's Michigan-made five-port power supply is a highly specific gift for the design obsessive in your life, but that's precisely why it'll hit.

Few things feel better than slipping into a plush robe at a fancy hotel, but honestly, most have nothing on Brooklinen's. Better yet, you don't need to spend $500 a night to get one.

Now that's one helluva coffee mug. Made from stainless steel with double-wall construction to keep it cool to the touch, this industrial number from Copenhagen-based design studio Service Projects comes with a generously proportioned saucer that does double duty as a serving tray.

John Waters warned against going home with someone who doesn't own books. I'd say the same rule goes for wine openers. And this one from Craighill really is the best.

You never know when you need a knife, pair of scissors, or a corkscrew—and now he'll never have to worry about missing any of those essential tools.

You could get him a candle. Or you could get him this handsome little contraption: a glass teardrop set in a brass cradle. Fill the glass with fragrance oil, light the tealight underneath, and voilà: instant home aura.

The most advanced vibe curators know: nothing sets the mood at home like well-crafted incense. Vyrao’s Verdant blend of bergamot, frankincense, and white musk packs a particularly calming punch as the seasons change.

Apple’s latest AirPods 3 refine a classic with noticeably better noise cancellation and a slick new live translation feature—proof the world’s best earbuds just keep getting smarter.

The new iPad mini gets its biggest glow-up yet, with a gorgeous 8.5-inch OLED display, the new A20 Pro chip, and a thinner, lighter build that's now water-resistant.

Some folks are organized, the rest of us have AirTags. The second-generation model improves the range, cranks up the speaker volume, and generally makes losing things less stressful.

Apple's brand-new HomeView brings the company's signature polish to the smart home, giving them a sleek new command center for everything from lights to thermostats.

Plenty of brands have tried their hand at recreating Sony's classic Walkman headphones, and now Sony itself is getting in on the action. The MDR-3R brings back that familiar retro look, this time with a USB-C connection.

Ray-Ban’s Audio Clubmasters pack open-ear audio and six built-in microphones into a classic frame. Best of all, he can enjoy the latest tech without making everyone wonder if they’re being filmed.

One of Nike ACG's most head-turning releases of the year, the Radical AirFlow shirt is a very good gift for the runner in your life, with a wild-looking, ultra-breathable fabric that'll make him look as cool as he feels.

Beat those sore muscles into submission so you can get back at it sooner rather than later.

#6644. 25 Midwestern Thanksgiving Recipes That Bring The Nostalgia (& The Flavor)

Even nicer than Midwest nice (and that's saying something!).

My holidays were split between regions growing up. We spent Thanksgiving at my dad’s side, and Christmas with my mom’s. With my mom’s Alabama and Texas roots and my dad's Missouri and Kansas roots, that meant that Christmas dinner was a Southern affair and Thanksgiving was a Midwestern feast. Both holiday spreads had a fair amount of overlap of dishes (casseroles galore), but I have to say: A classic Midwest Thanksgiving has a special place in my heart.

What makes a Midwest Thanksgiving, you may ask? All of the classics are present, plus a few surprising favorites that, in my house, no holiday is complete without. We think beyond the turkey, sometimes skip mashed potatoes for a cheesy casserole, and have to be careful not to fill up on all the rolls (butter and honey better be on the table). Ready to celebrate Midwest-style? Here are some recipes that your holiday won’t be complete without:

Made with canned pineapple, pistachio pudding, and Cool Whip, this retro crowd-pleasing dessert “salad” will take you straight back to the ’70s with just one bite. It’s the perfect recipe to throw together if you don’t have a ton of time, but you need to take something to that potluck or family gathering.

Thanksgiving is equally about food and football, so this tailgate-inspired stuffing is a no-brainer. Filled with beer cheese sauce and topped with crispy bacon, this twist on the classic holiday side is so irresistible, it’ll be gone long before halftime of that first Thanksgiving Day game.

It takes less than than 5 minutes to pour some pepper jelly over cream cheese and place some crackers around. These bites are slightly more elevated without many more steps. It’s for those that want to feel like they are putting some effort into their appetizer without it being difficult or time-consuming.

Don't be fooled by the name—the only thing deathly about this casserole is how absolutely delicious it is. This cheesy, creamy casserole is a staple at every holiday in my Kansas home, and Thanksgiving is no exception. Yes, we often have mashed potatoes too.

For this recipe, we ditched canned cream of mushroom soup and went for fresh instead. It's not how my mom makes it, but trust me—by sautéing mushrooms with sliced onion in butter, you're building a base with some serious depth of flavor. Cook the mushrooms enough that they get a little caramelized, and you'll really be good to go.

No matter the holiday, one thing is for sure: Deviled eggs will be making an appearance. Variations are always welcome (looking at you, harissa deviled eggs), but if grandpa is going to have a happy Thanksgiving, then this classic recipe better be present.

Strawberry pretzel tart, AKA strawberry pretzel salad, might sound a little strange, but trust us—it strikes the perfect balance of whimsical and classic, sweet and salty. The pretzel crust proves to be an ideal complement to the rich cream cheese layer and the sweet strawberries with their Jell-O glaze.

Turkey usually rules the roost at Thanksgiving, but it's not the only centerpiece present at many Midwestern holiday tables. Depending on how many family members are coming, my family has been known to prepare a turkey and a ham—it's the best of both worlds!

We’re certainly not opposed to roasted Brussels sprouts, but we also love giving them the traditional Thanksgiving treatment—plenty of butter, cream, and cheese. This method upgrades even the most humble vegetables while still allowing them to be the star of the show.

This sweet party dip is the perfect way to add that little extra something to your fruit spread, but your dipping options don't stop there! With just 5 minutes of prep, this is the easiest dessert that any party will be thankful for. Plus, you can easily make it ahead and travel with it, making it an ideal potluck recipe.

These Thanksgiving potato skins are piled high with leftovers, but they’re so good, they just might deserve a place in your holiday spread. The hollowed-out potatoes are an excellent vessel for extra-creamy mashed potatoes, stuffing, turkey, and dollops of cranberry sauce.

Essentially, this is chicken Alfredo, but with a few extra decadent add-ins, like cream cheese, garlic, and punchy spices like nutmeg and black pepper. When you’re craving the classic but have to serve a crowd, this is the recipe you should make.

A cheese ball is peak party appetizer nostalgia, and these cheese ball bites are here to put a new, shareable twist on the classic. They’re so simple to make, only require a handful of ingredients, and are super versatile based on what you have on hand.

I'll clarify that when I say stuffing, I'm actually referring to dressing. Traditional stuffing should be stuffed inside the turkey and cooked in there, but in my family, we've always called it stuffing. By cooking your stuffing in a baking dish, you get crunchy, buttery pieces of bread on top and soft, bread pudding-esque pieces underneath.

What’s the best kind of potato? A loaded baked potato, of course. With this in mind, we combined the two superstar spuds into one glorious dish. In it, light, airy mashed potatoes are topped with all of the classic baked potato fillings—cheddar cheese, chives, bacon, and sour cream—for a dish that truly embodies the best of both worlds.

Most sweet potato casseroles have only marshmallows or pecans. Don't even think about making this mistake. Topping with a pecan streusel and then marshmallows helps this Thanksgiving casserole stand out above all the rest.

If you’re not into creamy, melty macaroni and cheese with a wildly satisfying cheese-pull, then you might want to find another mac recipe. Sorry, but this slow-cooker macaroni and cheese is just too darn dreamy.

Step aside, all other casseroles—corn is not to be overlooked on the holiday table. If you prefer, drained and rinsed canned corn can be used instead of frozen, and you could substitute more milk in for the heavy cream. The finished casserole won't be quite as decadent, but it will still be delicious.

Deviled eggs are great, but when you have them for every holiday, it just makes sense to change them up sometimes. These are our new obsession

If green beans dressed up as cheesy garlic bread, then they would become these Parmesan roasted green beans. Tossed in garlic and black pepper and showered with cheese, this simply irresistible side dish will steal the spotlight at every holiday table.

This sweet party dip is the perfect way to add that little extra something to your fruit spread, but your dipping options don't stop there! With just 5 minutes of prep, this is the easiest dessert that any party will be thankful for.

#6643. The Secondhand Gifting Conundrum

Asking for a friend: would you be happy with a secondhand gift for Christmas?

In the current holiday preamble, shoppers are seeking out pre-loved luxury, and hopeful recipients are adding resale finds to their wishlists. While aspirational consumers seek more bang for their buck, top-end consumers favor one-of-a-kind pieces with a story to tell.

According to Rati Sahi Levesque, The RealReal CEO, gift shoppers are spending big and small this holiday season: designer accessories under $250 and collectible pieces over $10,000. “One of the things I love about resale is that great taste isn’t confined to a particular price point,” she says, explaining that shoppers can do more with less, or invest in something extraordinary for their recipient. “Resale gives you access to things that money alone can’t buy in the primary market.”

This November, Vinted searches for Christmas gifts were up 35% year on year, with interest building steadily since August, according to the platform. Similarly, on Depop, searches for “Christmas gifts” grew 248% year on year, climbing another 321% in the last month. The small luxuries category is building momentum for gifting, with searches for “Coachtopia” and “tall Uggs” up 132% and 96%, respectively, in the last month.

According to Deloitte’s holiday shopping report, 29% of US consumers may buy pre-owned luxury items as Christmas gifts this year. In the UK, 47% of 18 to 45-year-olds are willing to gift pre-loved items, per Ebay’s recent re-commerce report.

The pre-loved gifting surge is in line with broader growth in resale. In 2025, Boston Consulting Group and Vestiaire Collective estimated the global secondhand market’s value at $210-220 billion, forecasting a value of $320-$360 billion by 2030. As mentioned, value for money is a big draw, against a backdrop of inflation and a cost-of-living crisis. Vinted reports that the average adult fashion item sold on the platform is 72% less than RRP, while 69% of members believe Vinted gives them access to higher-quality or designer brands. For some shoppers, it’s also a way to resist the consumerism and waste associated with Christmas.

In this landscape, and as Gen Zs continue to favor messier, more eclectic and unique styling, gifting vintage is no longer niche. Nor is it easy. For gift-givers, pre-loved presents often involve more mental labor — either for the customer or their personal shopper. It requires skill to source a rarefied handbag or archival design — especially one in good condition.

As well as middle-income shoppers, high-net-worth individuals (HNWIs) are shopping secondhand this Christmas, with higher-ticket spending on rarefied goods. Sarah Jordan Buss, founder of The Vintage Project, a Beverly Hills boutique esteemed for high-profile clients, says that the budget for gifting usually sits around $1,000. Paris-founded resale platform Resee is also popular with HNWIs at Christmas. “The holiday gifting season is huge for us,” says co-founder and CEO Sofia Bernardin.

The rub? If shoppers are to nail that choice, platforms and sellers need to demonstrate that the gift has provenance, quality, authenticity and a story behind it. Competitors fighting for market share must sharpen their value proposition through personalization, product curation, clienteling, and strong certification measures.

For wealthy gifters, the process before the transaction is important. Evangeline Li is a high-net-worth curator based in London who often shops vintage accessories and jewelry to gift. She looks to 1990s Chanel, vintage Trifari and Mikimoto designs. Her spend bracket per gift is around £300-£1,000, depending on the person and piece. “I enjoy the hunt almost as much as the discovery itself,” she says, adding that she regularly visits antique markets in Britain, flea markets in Paris, and vintage stores in Japan, while also trawling Ebay, Etsy and Google.

Platforms report a strong interest in secondary market Chanel for Christmas gifting.

More recently, Li has become increasingly reliant on AI in her sourcing process. “It’s particularly useful when I’m searching for something unusual or difficult to describe as it can lead me to objects, designers and specialist dealers I might not otherwise have discovered,” she says.

For Li, it’s not just about designer names, but the historic and sentimental value. “I also enjoy finding gifts that are a little unexpected or playful: antique dice for friends who love games, a mid-century Tiffany & Co. double-deck playing card set in its signature blue box, or nostalgic collectibles such as Pokémon cards and vintage Hello Kitty dolls,” she says.

The RealReal’s Levesque concurs. “It doesn't have to be a big, recognizable logo. A vintage gold pendant for someone who loves layering jewelry or a beautiful Loro Piana belt for someone with a very understated wardrobe can feel much more personal than the obvious choice.” As she sees it, for affluent loved ones, the most desirable fashion items are pieces you can’t buy firsthand — they’re gifts the recipient might never have discovered.

When Buss is advising a client on a vintage gift, she has a few techniques to make it extra special. Often, she pulls a design from the year the intended recipient was born. “People really respond to that detail,” she says. Another technique is to consider small anecdotes the recipient might have made. “It might be a collection they mentioned in passing months ago or a piece from a designer they’ve loved for years — even something they regret getting rid of,” she says.

Resee also records an appetite for highly personalized luxury gifts. On the platform, the famous “Love” poster cards that Yves Saint Laurent would send to his collaborators annually have become a go-to gift during the holidays. Because they are dated — the series ran between 1970 and 2007 — gift givers choose specific designs with the same date as the recipient’s birth year. “It’s all about giving people something that feels as though it was specifically found for them,” says Bernardin. Of course, online, fakes and copies of these posters are rife, but Resee’s authentic poster cards come with the original postage stamps and shipping tubes, which offer a culturally richer gift. “I think the storytelling aspect is so important when it comes to giving a vintage gift,” Bernardin adds.

For Buss, bags are the most common gift clients request, and Chanel, Gucci and Chloé are some of the most popular brands. Often, the founder tells Vogue Business, she receives client requests for the original versions of bags that have been reissued, such as Saint Laurent’s Mombasa design and the Chloé Paddington, signaling the importance of provenance and cultural cachet. Secondhand marketplace 1stDibs is seeing traction on items such as Elsa Peretti’s Tiffany & Co. designs, Cartier watches, Hermès scarves, and iconic handbags and travel bags. Hard-to-find releases, such as Matthieu Blazy’s Chanel designs also perform well for gifting. “Buyers are gravitating toward classics that are easy to gift and easy to style, and that the recipient will cherish for years,” says Anthony Barzilay Freund, 1stDibs’s editorial director and director of fine art.

On The RealReal, consumers continue to spend healthily on household names: Hermès, Prada, Gucci, Cartier, Rolex and Tiffany & Co. “But what I find equally interesting is the appetite for pieces that are a little less expected,” says Levesque, pointing to momentum in emerging designers and distinctive finds — whether that’s a statement sweater from Zankov or collectible ornaments by artist Caroline Zimbalist. The executive also points to strong demand for archival pieces tied to specific designer eras, such as an Yves Saint Laurent Rive Gauche tassel belt from the 1970s or an embellished Chloé bag from the Phoebe Philo era.

Ebay also observes an interest in archival gifting. Kirsty Keoghan, Ebay’s general manager for fashion and luxury in Europe, highlights Prada’s sportier line, Linea Rossa, launched in 1997, as well as Pucci and Blumarine as big hits. She also calls out Karl Lagerfeld-era Chanel, John Galliano’s Dior and Tom Ford-era Gucci.

“Vintage is not a renewable resource and is thus the ultimate luxury,” says Mattie Barringer, co-founder of cult fashion and art label Women’s History Museum, which also runs a vintage boutique within the brand’s Canal Street store. The boutique’s esoteric range specializes in collectible items with fashion-historical value, spanning ’20s pumps through to ’90s Jean Paul Gaultier tops, as well as a selection of items under $100 for smaller budgets. “We feel an item or object with a life before really connects us to our shared humanity and history. What could be more Christmassy!”

While pre-loved gifting is gaining traction, shoppers can be put off by a few obstacles. Many of them are the same hangups associated with vintage in general. Where the thrill of the search remains important for many consumers, some are put off by the hassle and fear of landing a counterfeit. Here, platforms need to offer smoother shopping processes to unlock a larger portion of the market.

“Many shoppers still lack the confidence to complete a purchase because they are unsure whether they can trust the seller, the listing, or the protections available,” says Keoghan, encouraging shoppers to use Ebay’s authenticity and money-back guarantees where necessary. That way, “they can be absolutely certain that the gift they’ve picked out is going to be right,” she says.

This matters. In the gifting economy, platforms are competing with more traditional dealers, many of whom have longstanding relationships with their clients. The key criteria for discerning gift shoppers? “Condition is always my first consideration. I want a piece to be beautifully preserved, especially when I’m buying it as a gift,” says Li. “Beyond that, I really appreciate sellers who understand the history of their objects,” noting the importance of when something was made, how it was used, and what makes it interesting. Li is also hot on transparency, especially regarding authenticity and restorations that might have taken place on a given item. “I value dealers who are knowledgeable, honest, and genuinely passionate about what they sell,” she says.

In this vein, The RealReal offers a filtering function to streamline products that are “pristine” (new with tags), and the platform curates holiday gifting edits online and in-store that are informed by the brands, categories and pieces customers are most interested in by location. Additionally, the platform’s retail experts can offer personalized guidance for clients finding a gift based on the recipient’s taste, lifestyle and wardrobe.

“HNWIs are used to high-touch clienteling, discretion and access, so they expect private sourcing, authentication and care that feels closer to a luxury store than a resale feed,” says Sophy Vanner Critoph, strategy partner at creative agency Amplify. “Aspirational shoppers want speed, sharp cultural curation and zero friction: clear grading, fast delivery and a seamless experience that feels current and reliable.”

Resee’s inventory constantly shifts, but the focus remains on provenance and historical value.

Another issue for platforms to address? Shoppers with less fashion knowledge might be scared to buy something secondhand; the primary market has already been vouched for by a department store or a sales advisor. And if the gift isn’t right, vintage often involves more convoluted return processes, compared to the streamlined approach of online primary retail.

“We kept hearing women who would say, ‘I don’t want my husband to pick anything out for me. I just want him to give me something so I can buy myself something on Reiss,” says Bernardin. “So, we decided to do a vintage gift card.” Women’s History Museum Vintage also offers gift cards if the gift-giver isn’t confident in picking themselves. “There’s always an option to give the gift of a [vintage] shopping gift,” confirms Barringer. “In person, at our shop, via our website, or even Instagram.”

#6640. Popeyes Beat KFC In My Chicken Sandwich Showdown—But Can It Take Down Chick-fil-A?

The chicken sandwich wars are far from over.

Few fast food rivalries are as competitive as the battle for the best chicken sandwich. And while plenty of chains have introduced their own versions over the years, Chick-fil-A and Popeyes remain two of the biggest names in the conversation.

In my previous chicken sandwich showdown, I put KFC and Popeyes head-to-head to see which chain served the better sandwich. Popeyes ultimately came out on top, thanks to its bold seasoning, crispy breading, and well-balanced toppings. This time, I’m putting Popeyes up against one of its biggest competitors: Chick-fil-A.

Chick-fil-A has built its reputation around a simple, flavorful chicken sandwich that doesn’t need much to stand out. Popeyes, meanwhile, practically broke the internet when it introduced its now-famous chicken sandwich in 2019, sparking a fast food frenzy.

I ordered each chain’s original chicken sandwich to compare flavor, texture, juiciness, and overall balance. Both have their strengths, but only one can move on as my favorite.

Chick-fil-A’s Original Chicken Sandwich keeps things simple with a breaded chicken fillet, pickles, and a toasted bun.

Chick-fil-A’s chicken is so recognizable for a reason. The seasoning and brine give the fillet a savory, slightly tangy flavor that’s hard to beat, while the crispy breading contrasts nicely with the juicy chicken. The pickles also do their job, adding just enough acidity and crunch to balance out the richness.

My biggest complaint is that I wanted a little more from the sandwich. Compared to other fast food chicken sandwiches I’ve tried, many of which come with some type of sauce, Chick-fil-A’s original feels a bit plain. The chicken has enough flavor to stand on its own, but I think a little mayo or another sauce would have made the overall sandwich even better.

Still, there’s something to be said for a chicken sandwich that relies almost entirely on the quality and flavor of the chicken itself.

Popeyes’ Classic Chicken Sandwich features a breaded chicken fillet, pickles, mayo, and a toasted brioche bun. The sandwich that practically broke the internet when it launched in 2019 still lives up to the hype.

I’ve had this sandwich before where the chicken was slightly dry in spots, but thankfully that wasn’t the case this time. The fillet was juicy, flavorful, and incredibly well-seasoned. The breading had a satisfying crunch, and the bold, savory flavor made me want to keep going back for another bite.

The mayo was another important part of the sandwich, adding a tangy creaminess that complemented the chicken without overpowering it. Paired with the crisp pickles, it helped balance out the richness of the fried fillet.

I also really appreciated the proportions. The soft brioche bun held everything together without overwhelming the chicken, and each bite had a good balance of meat, breading, sauce, and pickles.

While Popeyes might not always deliver the most consistently juicy chicken, everything came together particularly well during this taste test. Between the seasoning, crispy breading, and well-balanced toppings, it’s easy to understand why this sandwich became such a phenomenon in the first place.

Popeyes already managed to beat KFC in my previous comparison, and after going up against Chick-fil-A, it’s keeping its winning streak alive.

Chick-fil-A arguably has the more distinctive chicken flavor, thanks to its savory, slightly tangy seasoning. But when I’m ordering a chicken sandwich, I want the entire thing to work together, and that’s where Popeyes has the advantage.

Chick-fil-A is still a great option, especially if you prefer a simpler sandwich that lets the chicken do most of the work. But after trying both, Popeyes delivered the better overall experience. With two wins under its belt, Popeyes is proving to be a pretty tough sandwich to beat.
